title: Align Miller-Urey / early-Earth atmosphere content with current consensus
question: What is the current scientific consensus on the early Earth atmosphere (weakly reducing/neutral vs strongly reducing), the relevance of Miller-Urey lightning conditions, and the impact-generated transient-reducing and locally-reduced prebiotic hypotheses — so the modules can frame the classic experiment as one model rather than the canonical early atmosphere?
why_now: MillerUreyExperiment.tsx defaults to the classic strongly-reducing CH4/NH3/H2O/H2 mix and asserts 'Deshalb hatte die frühe Erde keinen freien Sauerstoff'; EarlyEarthExperiment.tsx models a CO2-dominated atmosphere ('CO2 = Wärmespeicher'); OriginOfLifeTimeline.tsx presents Miller-Urey chemistry as the canonical early-Earth story. Current consensus has shifted to a weakly reducing/neutral CO2-N2-H2O atmosphere, with strongly reducing conditions only transient (post-impact) or local, so the modules currently teach a superseded assumption as fact — against MISSION.md's 'the science is real; the institution teaching it is not.'
